c-0: ^It's a matter of honor, branded. Something I wouldn't expect you to understand.

cutDownGaspar_1fa: ^*Gáspár meets your eyes with loathing.* I am no branded.

s: nop
^How are we going to get out of this crevice? It looks like the Lovashi have removed the ladder back to the camp.

^After you were pushed into the ravine, the Director continued his speech. Before he announced our pardon, a woman with a headdress shaped like the head of a spider appeared and ordered the Lovashi to attack us. That's why we're down here.

1cb: ^Do you really not know? The Vada are spirits that the Lovashi use to terrorize the Craft Folk on their lands. Sew discord, foment chaos, keep the serfs from trusting each other too much to rebel.

^Each one takes after a particular beast. That one must have been the Spider... Tawh-cache or something. 'The Weaver', they call her. I've heard she can take the form of other people, cast spells that make you unable to tell friend from foe, even curse you or your village just by being in her presence. Maybe all the Vada can. I don't know.

b: ^Takács. She can do all of that and more besides. The Vada were Táltos. *Gáspás searches for the words to explain.* Religious leaders. Like priests, but gifted with abilities beyond what we would consider normal.

s: ^'Were'? What happened to them?

c-0: ^I don't know, but what is clear is they are more spirit than human now; burden entities carried along bloodlines. A child born of the line of a Vada may become possessed by them, turning into one themselves. The possessed gains the knowledge of all of the memories of the Vada that takes hold of them, in essence becoming them.

s: ^She looked mostly human to me. What makes her so dangerous?
^How many other Vada are there?
^What was she doing here? This seems to be a strange place to meet something like her.
^She did something to the Lovashi. They weren't near so belligerent before she showed up.
^We have more important things to discuss right now.

c-0: ^I've heard of a few; Hound, Owl, Bear... Otter, Crow... Crane. I probably could think of a dozen if I had the time. A sage would be able to recall more; I doubt I've heard stories about them all.

b: ^The counts have many Vada at their beck and call. Our mission at this camp was important; so important that it's true purpose is known only to the Director and a select few others. Maybe it was important enough to warrant the supervision of one of the Vada as well.

^How should I know? The counts can command them somehow, that's why they're always bothering the Craft Folk and mostly leave the Lovashi be. Maybe one of the counts sent her here. For what purpose, I cannot say.

c-2: ^Yeah, you're right. I actually thought that we were going to get our pardon before the Director started talking about crushing the Lovashi's enemies. I'm not sure why, but she really did not want us to leave the camp alive.

b: ^I assumed you would not have been allowed to leave this camp until it's purpose was complete. If the Director meant to let you leave before then... *Gáspár looks troubled, and lost in thought.*

c-3: ^Yeah, like how to get out of here.

1da: ^Don't be fooled. The Vada are anything but human: they can't be killed. If you do manage to harm one, they just come back later. I've heard stories of when the Craft Folk killed a few back in the day; the Vada would eventually crawl out of the graves they were buried in to haunt the children of their slayer.

s: ^I saw a part of a face under that headdress she was wearing. How can you be sure they are the same creature, and not just some other person in a mask?

c-0: ^Most perplexing. I really can't say. Perhaps he changed his mind?
